youtube.baslik: Is sign language processed in the brain like a spoken language? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: A study published in 1996 found sign language aphasia in Deaf signers with left hemisphere damage; in signers with right hemisphere damage, sign language grammar was largely preserved despite visual and spatial difficulties. This shows that sign language is not a gesture system made of hand movements but a complete language that uses the brain's language networks; treating sign language as a second-class way of communicating is therefore wrong on scientific grounds too.
